note: Where a manufacturer's document and the per-opcode suite disagree, with what was measured and what this project does about it. Every entry was found by reading a data sheet in full and then going to the suite for the cases the document's claim would change. Some are settled by the recordings and say so; the ones that are not say what would settle them, rather than presenting a preference as a finding. Twice the document contradicts itself, and in both cases the passage that matches the silicon is the more specific one.

howToReadThis.suiteSays: What the recorded cycles show, with the case that shows it.
howToReadThis.whatThisProjectDoes: The behaviour in the code today, and why.
howToReadThis.whatWouldSettleIt: The measurement that would end the disagreement.
howToReadThis.status: open means a measurement on real silicon would still change what this project does. settled means the reasoning closes it and nothing further is needed. The open ones are collected in OPEN-QUESTIONS.md.
howToReadThis.severity: contradiction: a manufacturer printed one thing and the recordings show another. documentContradiction: one publisher saying two things. unstated: nobody wrote it down. unchecked: evidence exists somewhere but has not been run here.

divergences.subject: the data bank register after a software interrupt in emulation mode

documentSays.quote: In the Emulation mode, the PBR and DBR registers are cleared to 00 when a hardware interrupt, BRK or COP is executed. In this case, previous contents of the PBR are not automatically saved.

suiteSays.measured: All 10,000 emulation BRK tests, all 10,000 emulation COP tests and all 10,000 native BRK tests leave the data bank register exactly as they found it. 9,960 of the emulation BRK tests start with a non-zero data bank, so the cases that would show a clear are present and none of them shows one. The program bank is zero afterwards in all 30,000, which is the half of the sentence both sources agree on.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Clears the program bank and leaves the data bank alone, in both modes. The suite is the only evidence with a case count behind it, and the same caveat section is wrong about the native vector addresses and about which bank holds the (a,x) pointer, so its precision is not what its specificity suggests.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A program on a real part: set the data bank to something non-zero, drop into emulation mode, execute BRK, and have the handler push the data bank and read it back.
divergences.whyItMayNeverHaveMattered: In emulation mode the data bank is not pushed, so a part that cleared it would give an interrupt handler no way to restore it. Software written for that part would have had to reload the bank itself, which is what software does anyway.

andTheSamePublishersBookDoesNotRepeatIt.source: Programming the 65816, the BRK entry, printed page 338
andTheSamePublishersBookDoesNotRepeatIt.quote: 6502, 65C02, and Emulation Mode (e = 1): The program counter is incremented by two, then pushed onto the stack; the status register, with the b break flag set, is pushed onto the stack; the interrupt disable flag is set; and the program counter is loaded from the interrupt vector at $FFFE-FFFF.
andTheSamePublishersBookDoesNotRepeatIt.why: A step by step account of the same instruction in the same mode, by the same publisher, listing each thing the instruction does. The data bank register is not among them. Its native mode paragraph does name a bank register being cleared, the program bank, so the omission in the emulation paragraph is not the book being brief about banks in general.
andTheSamePublishersBookDoesNotRepeatIt.howMuchItSettles: Not outright. Silence in a programmer's account is weaker than a statement, and the book is describing what a programmer must know rather than enumerating every register the sequence touches. But it is a second rung one source that declines to repeat the caveat, which leaves the caveat as the only place the claim appears against 30,000 recorded cases and one other publication.

divergences.subject: whether a multi-byte pointer read out of the direct page stays inside the page, in emulation mode with the direct register page aligned

documentSays.quote: When in the Emulation mode, the direct addressing range is 000000 to 0000FF, except for [Direct] and [Direct],Y addressing modes and the PEI instruction which will increment from 0000FE or 0000FF into the Stack area.
documentSays.meaning: Three named exceptions leave the page and everything else wraps inside it.

suiteSays.howItWasMeasured: Every emulation-mode file for all five pointer modes and for PEI, 41 files and 410,000 tests, filtered to the cases where the direct register is page aligned and the pointer starts at the end of the page, then read straight off the recorded cycle addresses.

cases.verdict: left the page, which the document says it should not
left the page, which the document says it should
wrapped inside the page, which the document says it should not

cases.test: the case at D=000C00 with an operand of FF
cases.verdict: wrapped inside the page, which the document says it should not

suiteSays.notCovered: (d) and (d),y. The suite contains no emulation case for either where the direct register is page aligned and the pointer starts at FE or FF, so nothing measured constrains them.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Follows the four measured cases exactly, and takes the document for the two the suite does not cover, which means (d) and (d),y wrap. The document's exception list is right about one of the four cases it covers, so it is not treated as a rule here, only as evidence where there is nothing else.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Six short programs on a real part, one per mode, each with the direct register page aligned and a pointer at FF, reading back the byte the part fetched. Until then this project's behaviour for (d) and (d),y is a document reading rather than a measurement, and is marked as such.
divergences.whyItIsOddEitherWay: No simple rule produces the measured set. Whatever the part does, it is not deciding by pointer width and it is not deciding by whether the mode is one the 6502 had.

divergences.subject: which address the NMOS 6502 puts on the bus during a taken branch

documentSays.quote: T2* PC + 2 + offset (w/o carry), OP CODE, R/W 1, Offset Added to Program Counter; T3** PC + 2 + offset (with carry), OP CODE, R/W 1, Carry Added. *Skip if branch not taken. **Skip if branch not taken; skip if branch operation doesn't cross page boundary.
documentSays.readFrom: The scanned page A-13, read as an image rather than through the text layer, so this is what the manual prints rather than an artefact of the scan.

suiteSays.measured: A taken branch that stays inside its page spends its third cycle reading the instruction it is not going to run, at PC+2. A taken branch that leaves its page spends a fourth cycle at PC+2 with the offset added to the low byte only. So the address the manual gives for the third cycle is what the fourth cycle carries, and the address it gives for the fourth cycle never appears on the bus at all.

cases.verdict: third cycle at PC+2, and the branch went to 00907F
third at PC+2, fourth at the low-byte-only sum, and the branch went to 00781F

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Follows the recording: a dead read at PC+2 on any taken branch, and a second at the low-byte-only sum when the page changes. Every one of the 2,440,000 non-halting cases in the suite agrees, including 40,000 branch cases, which the manual's reading would fail.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing needs settling about the behaviour. What is unsettled is whether the manual's two rows were transposed in print or describe an earlier part, and only a run on real silicon of that vintage would say.
divergences.whyItMatters: A model built from the manual alone puts the wrong address on the bus on every taken branch, which is invisible in a state comparison and visible to any device that watches its own address lines.

divergences.subject: which address a CMOS 65C02 puts on the bus during its spare cycles, and how long three of its instructions take

documentSays.quote: Indexed addressing across page boundary: NMOS 6502, extra read of invalid address; W65C02S, extra read of last instruction byte. Read/Modify/Write instruction at effective address: NMOS 6502, one read and two write cycles; W65C02S, two read and one write cycle. Jump indirect, operand = XXFF: NMOS 6502, page address does not increment; W65C02S, page address increments, one additional cycle. Flags after decimal operation: NMOS 6502, invalid N, V and Z flags; W65C02S, valid flags. One additional cycle.
documentSays.note: Every one of those is exactly what the recordings show, and the model follows all of them. The caveats table is the reliable part of this document.
documentSays.andYetTable6_5: The timing chart in the same document gives different addresses for three of those spare cycles: the half-formed address for an indexed access, the address after the target for a read-modify-write, and PC+2 for both indirect jumps. All three are contradicted by the caveats table above and by the recordings.

suiteSays.measured: 7,630,080 cases agree with the caveats table, cycle for cycle. Two printed figures do not survive, and both are counts rather than addresses.

cases.printed: 3 bytes, 8 cycles, in the invalid-OpCode table of Table 7-1
cases.measured: 4 cycles, in all 10,000 cases of all three suites: the opcode, its two operand bytes, and one spare cycle re-reading the second operand
cases.verdict: the only invalid opcode whose printed cycle count the recordings contradict; the other six rows of that table match exactly

cases.mode: read-modify-write of an indexed absolute address inside one page
cases.printed: Read/Modify/Write instructions absolute indexed in same page: NMOS 6502 seven cycles, W65C02S six cycles
cases.measured: Six for ASL, LSR, ROL and ROR, and seven for INC and DEC, in all three suites: 4,966 of 10,000 ASL cases take seven because the index crossed a page, and all 10,000 DEC cases take seven whether it crossed or not
cases.verdict: the printed row is right for four of the six instructions it covers and wrong for the other two

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Follows the caveats table where it speaks, which is everywhere the timing chart disagrees with it, and follows the recordings for the two counts above. Which means: the spare cycle of an indexed access re-reads the last byte of the instruction, a read-modify-write reads twice and writes once, an indirect jump spends its extra cycle on the address the older part's page-wrap bug would have used, decimal arithmetic costs a cycle, $5C takes four cycles rather than eight, and increment and decrement of an indexed absolute address always pay for indexing while the shifts and rotates pay only across a page.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: For the two counts, a logic analyser on a real part running $5C and running DEC $2000,X with an index that stays inside the page. Nothing else here needs settling: the document's own caveats table and the recordings agree.
divergences.whyTheTimingChartIsNotFollowed: Because the same document contradicts it twice over, in Table 7-1 and in the recordings, and because a chart that gives a spare cycle the wrong address is the kind of error that survives review: nothing in a state comparison can see it.

divergences.subject: the address of the extra cycle a CMOS 65C02 spends on decimal arithmetic

alsoSays.quote: Note that when VDA and VPA are both low, invalid addresses may be generated. The Page and Bank addresses could also be invalid.
alsoSays.section: 8.5 VDA and VPA Valid Memory Address Output Signals

documentSays.section: Table 7-1 Microprocessor Operational Enhancements, the Flags after decimal operation row
documentSays.note: This replaced a citation to Table 6-5 note 6 of this data sheet, which has no Table 6-5: its tables run 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 5-1, 5-2, 6-1 to 6-4 and 7-1. The sixteen bit sheet does have one, which is where that number came from. The row quoted here is the same part's own statement of the extra cycle, and unlike the old one it is a contiguous sentence a search can find.

suiteSays.measured: Every recorded decimal ADC and SBC spends its extra cycle reading 00007F, whatever the program counter, the operands or the flags are. Four cases at four different program counters all carry 00007F.

cases.verdict: a constant, and therefore not an address the part computed

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Spends the extra cycle, and points it at the operand address rather than at the constant the recording carries. A decimal add on a 65c02 or a w65c02 takes three cycles here where the same add takes two on a 6502, which is the part the document settles. The address it drives is the one the part last had on the bus, because the document says an internal cycle's address may be invalid and the recording carries a placeholder rather than a measurement. conformance/cycles.py leaves that one cycle out of the comparison, narrowly and by opcode, and prints how many it left out.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A logic analyser on a real W65C02S during a decimal add. Until then the extra cycle is real and its address is not evidence, and a model that reproduced 00007F would be reproducing the recorder rather than the part.
divergences.whyItIsRecordedNow: So that nobody tries to derive 00007F from the state, and so that the one cycle the runner does not compare is a stated exception rather than a silence.

divergences.subject: the address on the bus during the discarded read of an indexed access

documentSays.quote: T3 ADL: BAL + index register / ADH: BAH + C. Carry is 0 or 1 as required from previous add operation.
documentSays.section: Appendix A, tables A.2.5, A.2.7, A.3.4 and A.4.4

andAlsoSays.quote: T4 ADL: BAL + Y / ADH: BAH. Data (Discarded).
andAlsoSays.why: The same cycle of the same kind of access, written without the carry two pages later. The appendix gives the discarded read two different addresses.
andAlsoSays.inASecondPrinting: Synertek reprinted the same appendix under its own name, and both forms appear there unchanged, on the same page numbers. Two publishers printed the same inconsistency, so it is the document rather than a slip in one copy.

suiteSays.measured: Every crossing case in the suite puts the base high byte on the bus for that cycle, never the corrected one. If the corrected address were driven there, the read would land on the right byte and the appendix's own footnote, which says the data fetched in T3 is ignored when the page is crossed, would have nothing to ignore.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Drives the base high byte with the index added only to the low byte, which is the A.3.6 form. That is the reading the suite carries, the reading the footnote in the other four tables requires, and the reading under which a store to a hardware register does not touch a second register one page below the one it names.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A program on a real part: point an indexed store at an address one byte below a page boundary so the index crosses it, put a memory-mapped register at the uncorrected address, and see whether the register is read.
divergences.whyItMatters: This is the cycle that makes an indexed store to a hardware register dangerous. A reader who took the BAH + C form would model the discarded read as landing on the same address as the write, and would miss the spurious access one page below it that real programs have to work around.

divergences.subject: which cycle of a taken branch carries which address

documentSays.quote: T2 PC + 2 + offset (w/o carry), Offset Added to Program Counter. T3 PC + 2 + offset (with carry), Carry Added.

suiteSays.measured: Every taken branch drives the unmodified program counter on its third cycle. In four hundred cases checked with a non-zero offset that stay inside a page, the third address is PC + 2 exactly, never PC + 2 + offset. On a crossing branch the fourth cycle carries PC + 2 + offset without carry, which is the address the table prints one row higher, and the corrected target is not reached until the opcode fetch of the next instruction.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Drives the counter on the third cycle and the partially corrected address on the fourth, so both addresses appear one row later than the table prints them and the corrected target never appears inside the branch at all.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A program on a real part: place a branch so its target is on the next page, put a memory-mapped register at the partially corrected address, and see on which cycle it is read.
divergences.whyItMatters: The table has one row for each of three cycles, so it reads as though the offset is on the bus a cycle before it is. Anything counting bus activity, a cycle-exact video timing model or a bus analyser trace, comes out a cycle early on every taken branch.

divergences.subject: the stack addresses of a pull, written as plain sums

documentSays.quote: T3 Stack Ptr. + 1. T4 Stack Ptr. + 2. T5 Stack Ptr. + 3.
documentSays.section: Appendix A, tables A.5.2, A.5.5 and A.5.7

suiteSays.measured: A return from interrupt entered with the stack pointer at FE reads 01FE, 01FF, 0100 and 0101. The sums in the table would give 01FF, 0200 and 0201.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Keeps every stack access inside page one, which is what the part does and what the body of the same manual says elsewhere. The sums in the appendix hold everywhere except across the page edge, so they are read as shorthand rather than as arithmetic.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing outstanding. The stack living in page one is stated in the body of the same document and is not in question; only the appendix's notation is loose.
divergences.whyItMatters: A pull that starts near the top of the stack is exactly the case a program hits after a deep sequence of pushes, so a model built from the appendix alone would read four bytes from the wrong page at the moment it matters most.

divergences.subject: the page-crossing cycle on the indirect indexed rows of AND and ORA

documentSays.section: Appendix B, pages B-3 and B-20

andAlsoSays.quote: AND Oper, X  3D  3  4*. ORA Oper, X  1D  3  4*. * Add 1 if page boundary is crossed.
andAlsoSays.why: Both instructions carry the mark on their absolute indexed rows, on the same page as the row that lacks it, so the omission is one row rather than a claim about the instruction. The six other Group One instructions carry it on all three indexed rows.
andAlsoSays.section: Appendix B, the same two pages

suiteSays.measured: Both take six cycles when the index carries out of the low byte and five when it does not, which is what ADC, CMP, EOR, LDA and SBC do on the same addressing mode. Nothing in the suite separates these two from those five.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Takes the extra cycle on all eight, because the addressing mode is the same one and the cycle comes from re-reading at the corrected address rather than from the operation.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing outstanding. The two instructions share their addressing hardware with six that are printed correctly, and the same appendix marks their absolute indexed rows.
divergences.whyItMatters: A timing budget built by adding up the printed counts comes out one cycle short every time one of these two crosses a page, which on a machine whose video timing is counted in cycles is the difference between a stable picture and a torn one.

divergences.subject: how many cycles the reserved opcode 5C spends on a CMOS part

documentSays.quote: All are NOP's (reserved for future use). OpCode 5C, Bytes 3, Cycles 8.
documentSays.section: Table 7-1, the Execution of invalid OpCodes row

suiteSays.corpus: SingleStepTests 65x02, the wdc65c02, synertek65c02 and rockwell65c02 sets
suiteSays.measured: Ten thousand cases per part, thirty thousand in all, and every one of them is four cycles: the opcode, the two operand bytes, and the second operand byte read again. No case anywhere in the three sets shows eight.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Takes four, because that is the only shape any source states. The data sheet gives a count and no addresses, so following it would mean inventing four bus cycles nobody has written down, and inventing them is worse than recording that they are unknown. The other forty-three reserved opcodes match the same table exactly, which is why this one is treated as a single open question rather than as a reason to distrust the row.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A logic analyser on a real W65C02S executing 5C, which would give both the count and the four addresses the data sheet does not print. Nothing short of that can be implemented, because a count alone is not a bus trace.
divergences.whyItMatters: Four cycles of difference on an opcode no program deliberately executes matters only where a program runs off into unwritten memory, which is a crash either way. It is recorded because it is the one place in the reserved-opcode row where the part and the page disagree, and because a reader who trusts the row deserves to know which entry to check.

divergences.subject: which address the modify cycle and the push drive when the register is eight bits

documentSays.quote: 1d. Absolute (R-M-W) a, cycle 5: DBR,AA+1, IO. 22c. Stack s, cycle 3: 0,S-1, REG Low.

suiteSays.measured: With an eight bit register the modify cycle of a read-modify-write is at AA and the push is at S. The addresses the table prints appear only when the register is sixteen bits, which is the case where the lettered row directly above them is also present.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Drives the last byte actually accessed, which is AA and S in the narrow form and AA+1 and S-1 in the wide one. The table has only the wide form of these five rows.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing outstanding. The narrow form follows from the rows above it: a cycle cannot sit on the byte after one that was never read.
divergences.whyItMatters: Five rows of a table that is otherwise complete have no eight bit form, so a reader building a narrow register model from the page alone puts the modify cycle and the push one byte off. Four come out a byte high and the push a byte low, because the stack grows the other way.

divergences.subject: whether the new program counter of an indexed indirect jump is a program address

documentSays.quote: 2a. Absolute Indexed Indirect (a,x), cycle 5: VDA 0, VPA 1, PBR,AA+X, New PCL.

andAlsoSays.quote: 3b. Absolute Indirect (a), cycle 4: VDA 1, VPA 0, 0,AA, New PCL.
andAlsoSays.why: The same operation, reading a new program counter through a pointer, marked the other way two groups later. The two differ only in which bank holds the pointer: the program bank for the indexed form, bank zero for the plain one.

suiteSays.measured: Every recorded case of both opcodes marks those cycles a valid data address and not a valid program address, which is the same way the recordings mark the plain indirect jump.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Marks them a data address, following the recordings and the table's own treatment of the plain indirect jump. The table's other reading is defensible, since the pointer of the indexed form really does live in the program bank, but nothing else in the table draws that distinction and nothing recorded supports it.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A logic analyser on the VPA and VDA pins of a real W65C816S executing JMP (a,x). Those pins exist precisely so a system can tell the two apart, so the answer is directly observable on hardware and on nothing less.
divergences.whyItMatters: A system that qualifies its memory map with these pins, which is what they are for, would route those two fetches to program memory rather than to data memory. On a machine where the two are different devices that is the difference between a jump that works and one that does not.
divergences.andTheSamePublisherTransposesThemElsewhe: Appendix C of Programming the 65816, which the same company holds the copyright to, prints the four qualifier states under headers in the opposite order from the data sheet's, so that a valid program address comes out as the Valid Data Address pin high and the Valid Program Address pin low. That is a transposition of exactly these two signals in this publisher's own documentation. It does not settle this entry, but it is the reason a single printed row is not enough to overturn thirty thousand recorded cases.

divergences.subject: what a reset drives on the bus during its six delay cycles

documentSays.quote: When the line goes high, the microprocessor will delay 6 cycles and then fetch the new program count vectors from specific locations in memory (PCL from location FFFC and PCH from location FFFD).

suiteSays.measured: Nothing. Every case in every suite starts with the part already running and the registers set by the test, so no recording covers a reset at all. This is the manufacturer's statement standing alone.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Charges all eight cycles: the six the manual names and the two of the vector fetch. They appear in `cycles`, so a host pacing against a real clock is not six cycles ahead of the wall after every reset. They do not appear in `trace`, because every cycle of this part drives an address and no source on hand names the six driven here.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A recording of the reset sequence, which no published corpus carries. The count is not in question and is now modelled; what is missing is the address on the bus during those six cycles. Six invented addresses would read as knowledge, so the gap is left visible as the one place where `cycles` counts more than `trace` records.
divergences.whyItMatters: A device that decodes the address bus sees six accesses this model cannot describe. The timing a host pays is now right; the picture of what the bus carried is absent rather than wrong, and those are different failures.

divergences.subject: how many cycles STP and WAI cost on a W65C02

documentSays.quote: Uses 3 cycles to shut the processor down; additional cycles are required by reset to restart it
documentSays.section: including the 6502, 65C02 and 65802, WDC, instruction tables for STP and WAI

suiteSays.measured: Nothing. The files for DB and CB hold no cases at all, because a part that stops its own clock produces no recording to compare against.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Charges three cycles on the 65816, matching the book, and two on the W65C02. The book's tables mark both instructions as available to the 65802 and 65816 and not to the 65C02, so its three-cycle note is not a statement about the W65C02, and the W65C02S data sheet gives no cycle count for either instruction in the text available here.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: The cycle-count column of the W65C02S data sheet's operation table, which is a graphic in the copy on hand and did not survive text extraction, or any recording of a W65C02 executing DB or CB.
divergences.whyItMatters: A part told to STP halts its own clock, so the count is the last thing a host is charged before time stops for that processor. It is one cycle either way and it is the kind of gap that stays invisible until somebody counts.

divergences.subject: what a halted W65C02 holds on its address lines

documentSays.quote: A negative transition to the low state prior to the falling edge of PHI2 will halt the microprocessor with the output address lines reflecting the current address being fetched. This assumes the processor setup time is met. This condition will remain through a subsequent PHI2 in which the ready signal is low. The WAI instruction pulls RDY low signaling the WAit-for-Interrupt condition, thus RDY is a bi-directional pin.

suiteSays.measured: Nothing. The files for CB and DB hold no cases. The 65816 suite does carry 40,000, and they show something different for that part: no address at all and every output line inactive, which is what this project models there.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Charges the time and records no bus activity. A W65C02 held this way is holding an address rather than fetching one, and this project's trace records accesses rather than the state of lines, so it has no way to say 'the address bus still reads $8001 and nothing is happening'. The cycle count is right and the bus picture is absent rather than wrong.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Not evidence but a decision: a trace that recorded line states rather than accesses could express a held bus, and would change what every other cycle in this project means. Recordings of a real W65C02 during WAI would say which address it settles on, which the data sheet leaves as 'the current address being fetched'.
divergences.whyItMatters: A device watching the address bus of a waiting part sees a held address, not a quiet bus. Anything decoding that address, a chip select that stays asserted, behaves differently from anything decoding nothing.

divergences.subject: whether a two cycle opcode turns its internal cycle into a bus read when an interrupt is pending

documentSays.quote: Nothing. The data sheet does not describe what an internal cycle does differently while an interrupt is waiting to be taken.

suiteSays.measured: Nothing. Every case runs one instruction with no pin asserted, so no recording in any published corpus covers an instruction executed while an interrupt is pending.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Spends an ordinary internal cycle, with no dependence on whether an interrupt is waiting. Two widely used implementations do something else: ares and bsnes replace that cycle with a read of the program counter, without incrementing it, for a named list of two cycle opcodes covering the flag instructions, the register transfers, the increments and decrements, the shifts and rotates, NOP and XCE.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: A logic capture of a real part executing one of those opcodes with the interrupt line already low. An implementation is a lead rather than an authority here: ares and bsnes share one lineage, so their agreement is one source and not two, and neither ships the measurement behind the behaviour.
divergences.whyItMatters: A device watching the bus sees a read that this model does not perform, at the exact moment an interrupt is being taken. It changes nothing a program can compute, and everything a cycle for cycle comparison against real hardware would show.

divergences.subject: the transistor level simulation that could settle most of the NMOS questions, and why it is not being used

documentSays.quote: Nothing. This is about a source rather than about the part, so there is no document to name and none is named.

suiteSays.measured: A transistor level simulation of the 6502 die is public and has been used as an oracle by others: MAME's NMOS 6502 opcode definitions carry the note 'Verified with visual6502'. It answers the questions a data sheet drawn at cycle resolution and a recording written one row per cycle cannot, which is what a discarded read puts on the bus and which cycle of a branch carries which address.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Neither. Nothing here has been run against it. Every entry above that says a logic capture would settle it still says so, and this would be the nearest thing to one that needs no bench.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Running it. The same work is already recorded for the Z80 in the other repository of this family, where a port of the Z80Explorer netlist resolver was written and does not converge. Whether the 6502 simulation is easier to drive is unknown here, because it has not been tried.
divergences.whyItMatters: It is the one route to closing several open questions at once without buying hardware, and the parts it would answer for are the NMOS ones where the documents are oldest and the recordings least explained.

divergences.subject: how long a reset takes, which two manufacturers give differently

documentSays.quote: MOS: 'the microprocessor will delay 6 cycles and then fetch the new program count vectors'. WDC: 'When a positive edge is detected, there will be a reset sequence lasting seven clock cycles.'

suiteSays.measured: Nothing. Every case begins with the part already running and its registers set by the test, so no recording in any published corpus covers a reset.

divergences.whatThisProjectDoes: Charges each part what its own manufacturer states. Eight on the NMOS parts, which is the six-cycle delay plus the two of the vector fetch, and seven on the W65C02S. Rockwell and Synertek state no count for their CMOS parts, so those keep the figure of the design they are built from rather than borrowing WDC's, and WDC states none for the sixteen bit parts, so those do the same. The figure is a property of the model rather than of the family.
divergences.whatWouldSettleIt: Whether the two figures describe different silicon or one loose sentence. They are one cycle apart and neither manufacturer mentions the other's part. A logic capture of a reset on an NMOS 6502 and on a W65C02S would say whether the difference is real, and no published corpus carries a reset at all.
divergences.whyItMatters: Only for a host counting cycles across a reset, which happens once at power on. It is one cycle, and it is one cycle this project would have got wrong on the WDC part by assuming a family shares a figure that only one of its manufacturers ever printed.
